propositions: Closing a ticket triggers compaction via _compact_on_close, which acquires the store write lock and holds it for minutes while folding events, taking snapshots, retiring sources, and running git operations, starving concurrent writers.

The compaction hold is unbounded and can reach 13+ minutes (measured 13m53s), while other close operations take only seconds, because _compact_locked takes the write lock for its entire fold with no time limit on the hold itself.

Compaction is optional housekeeping (not a correctness requirement) and already exists as a standalone command (rebar compact <id>), so removing it from the close path restores short lock holds while preserving the ability to compact on demand.

The removal of _compact_on_close as an inline trigger in the close path is safe because unfolded event logs remain valid and reducible; the git commit log simply contains no ticket: COMPACT commit until compaction is explicitly triggered elsewhere.
